[dev-instance] warning:   every value in compose.yaml is written '${NAME:-default}', and Debian trixie's
[dev-instance] warning:   podman-compose does not apply the part after ':-'. Where it does not, the placeholder text
[dev-instance] warning:   itself reaches the containers — the application refuses to start and the database cannot
[dev-instance] warning:   initialise. The check below settles it for this host rather than guessing.
[dev-instance] warning:   'cp .env.example .env' assigns every one of them, and is what §2 asks for on any host

[compose-substitution]   What that costs, from the run that found it: the application refuses to start and names
[compose-substitution]   five of them; POSTGRES_USER reaches initdb as punctuation, so the database never
[compose-substitution]   initialises and crash-loops; and the rest are wrong in silence — RESTAURANT_NAME renders
[compose-substitution]   the placeholder as the restaurant's name, an unparseable integer is indistinguishable from
[compose-substitution]   an absent one, and OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT arrives non-empty, which turns the exporter
[compose-substitution]   ON and points it at a hostname made of braces.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   Two remediations, in order:
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]     1. cp .env.example .env
[compose-substitution]        Every variable compose.yaml interpolates is assigned in that file, so nothing is left
[compose-substitution]        depending on a default. Then run this check again — it will tell you whether it was
[compose-substitution]        enough on your engine, which is not something this repository can know for you.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]     2. Use a compose that applies defaults:
[compose-substitution]          podman compose …            the Docker Compose provider, if it is installed
[compose-substitution]          pipx install podman-compose a newer release than the distribution's
[compose-substitution]        or export the variables in the shell that runs the stack.
[compose-substitution] 
[compose-substitution]   Do not run an instance you care about on an engine that fails this check. Only five of the
[compose-substitution]   affected settings are ones this application validates; the others do not announce themselves.

kushal@virginia:~/src/dotnet/myrestaurant$ cat .env
# Copy to `.env` and adjust. `.env` is git-ignored; never commit a populated one.
# Configuration is environment-only (TECHNICAL_SPECIFICATION §13). Every value here has a safe dev
# default in the app; the ones marked "PRODUCTION: change" MUST be overridden before going live.

# --- Identity & origin ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
RESTAURANT_NAME=My Restaurant
# The canonical origin for QR/link URLs and the fallback for the WebAuthn RP ID. Dev uses Caddy on
# 8443; production is your Cloudflare named-tunnel hostname (a stable domain so passkeys persist).
# PRODUCTION: change (must be an https URL). The RP ID is derived per request from the host the
# browser is on (ADR-0005), so a quick tunnel's per-run *.trycloudflare.com host works too — this
# value is the fallback when a request carries no trusted Origin header.
RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN=https://localhost:8443
# Wildcard origins (besides RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN and loopback) allowed to act as the WebAuthn
# relying party (ADR-0005, §3.3). Comma/space/newline separated; each is scheme://host with an
# optional single leading "*." label, https, no path or port. The default trusts Cloudflare quick
# tunnels so `scripts/quick_tunnel.sh` demos work with passkeys out of the box; clear it (set to a
# single space) to lock passkeys to RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN only.
RESTAURANT_TRUSTED_ORIGIN_PATTERNS=https://*.trycloudflare.com
# The restaurant's IANA zone. EVERY instant the application renders — order times, the footer clock,
# an administrator's audit column — is shown in this zone, for every viewer, wherever they are (§8.1).
# A guest abroad checking last week's bill sees the times the meal actually happened at.
RESTAURANT_TIME_ZONE=America/New_York
# How those times are written: "12-hour" (3:04 PM) or "24-hour" (15:04). Display only; it decides
# nothing about what is stored. Before this existed the choice came from whatever locale the container
# image happened to carry, which is to say from nobody (F-36).
RESTAURANT_CLOCK_FORMAT=12-hour
RESTAURANT_CURRENCY_CODE=USD
# Where this instance's source code is published (§11.9). Linked from /source, which the footer of
# every page links to. If you have MODIFIED this program and run it as a network service, AGPL-3.0-only
# §13 requires you to offer your users the corresponding source — point this at your fork and you have
# done so:
#
#     RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL=https://git.example.com/you/myrestaurant
#
# Absolute http or https; http is accepted here (unlike RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN) so a self-hosted
# forge on a LAN is not refused.
#
# ASSIGNED EMPTY, and that is F-50's ruling applied to this file rather than an omission. Empty means
# "the program's own default", which is RestaurantOptions.DefaultSourceUrl and the ONE place the
# fallback is written down — the reason compose.yaml passes this variable through with an empty default
# too. This file previously spelled the upstream URL here, which is the same defect one layer over: a
# fork whose first edit is that constant would have had it silently overridden by the `.env` they were
# told to copy, and served their users a §13 offer pointing at somebody else's repository.
RESTAURANT_SOURCE_URL=

# --- Database ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Consumed by the postgres container. PRODUCTION: change POSTGRES_PASSWORD.
POSTGRES_USER=myrestaurant
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=myrestaurant
POSTGRES_DB=myrestaurant
# The app's own connection string. In compose this is derived from the POSTGRES_* values above and
# points at the `postgres` service; only set this if you are pointing at an external database.
# RESTAURANT_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING=Host=postgres;Port=5432;Database=myrestaurant;Username=myrestaurant;Password=myrestaurant

# --- Data protection keys (§3.4) -----------------------------------------------------------------
# A named volume in compose; back it up alongside the database or TOTP secrets/cookies are lost.
DATA_PROTECTION_KEYS_DIRECTORY=/var/lib/myrestaurant/dataprotection

# --- Timing knobs --------------------------------------------------------------------------------
KITCHEN_SUBMISSION_REMINDER_SECONDS=60   # §10.2, min 1
TABLE_JOIN_TOKEN_ROTATION_SECONDS=60     # §4.3, min 10
TABLE_JOIN_GRANT_MINUTES=10              # §4.4, min 1
TABLE_DISPLAY_PAIRING_CODE_MINUTES=10    # §4.2, min 1

# --- Argon2id (§3.2 + startup floor guard) -------------------------------------------------------
# The app refuses to start below the floor: memory >= 19456 KiB, iterations >= 2, parallelism >= 1.
ARGON2_MEMORY_KIBIBYTES=65536
ARGON2_ITERATIONS=3
ARGON2_PARALLELISM=1
ARGON2_MAX_CONCURRENT_HASHES=4

# --- Backups (§15) -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# A backup set is TWO files sharing one timestamp: the database dump and the Data Protection key ring
# (myrestaurant-<stamp>.dump and myrestaurant-<stamp>-dataprotection.tar). Without the ring, every
# stored TOTP secret is undecryptable — the accounts come back and the enrolled authenticators do not
# (OPERATIONS §6 and §8). scripts/backup.sh writes both, scripts/restore.sh puts both back, and
# scripts/restore_drill.sh rehearses the round trip against a scratch database it creates and
# destroys — it never writes to this one.
BACKUP_DIRECTORY=/var/lib/myrestaurant/backups
BACKUP_SCHEDULE_TIME=03:30
BACKUP_RETENTION_COUNT=14
# The backup and restore scripts find the postgres and web containers by name and REFUSE when more
# than one matches, because dumping the wrong database looks exactly like success. Set these to skip
# discovery — required in CI, and useful whenever a second postgres container is around (the drill
# starts one on purpose).
# POSTGRES_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_postgres_1
# WEB_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_web_1
# Which container engine scripts/backup.sh and scripts/restore_drill.sh use. Unset is right on a host
# with one engine. On a host with BOTH — every GitHub Actions runner is one, since its image installs
# a static podman bundle next to Docker — the two scripts differ in what they can work out for
# themselves: backup.sh asks each engine whether it can see the container it was told to dump and uses
# the one that can, while the drill creates its own container and so has nothing to infer from. Set
# this when the containers you mean belong to a specific engine (F-43).
# CONTAINER_ENGINE=podman
# The scratch image the drill restores into. Fully qualified so a short-name registry prompt cannot
# hang an unattended run.
# DRILL_POSTGRES_IMAGE=docker.io/library/postgres:17-alpine

# --- OpenTelemetry (optional, §12) ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Empty by default; when empty the app attaches no OTLP exporter (no connection-refused noise). Fill
# these in to export — for example OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=https://otlp.example.com and
# OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=authorization=Bearer <token>.
#
# ASSIGNED EMPTY RATHER THAN COMMENTED OUT (F-57), and that matters more here than anywhere else in
# this file. Every variable compose.yaml interpolates must be assigned, because on an engine that does
# not apply the default after ':-' — Debian trixie's podman-compose does not — a commented-out line
# leaves the placeholder text to reach the container. An EMPTY endpoint switches the exporter off; the
# literal string `${OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT:-}` is not empty, so it switches the exporter ON and
# points it at a hostname made of braces. scripts/check_compose_substitution.sh tells you whether your
# engine needs this file at all.
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS=
OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=myrestaurant
# run.sh also accepts a legacy UPTRACE_DSN and translates it into the OTEL_* variables above.
# UPTRACE_DSN=

# --- Production tunnel (production profile only, §14.1) ------------------------------------------
# PRODUCTION: set to your Cloudflare named-tunnel token. Required by `--profile production`; empty
# here, and assigned rather than commented out for the reason recorded beside the OTEL_* pair (F-57).
CLOUDFLARE_TUNNEL_TOKEN=

# --- Detached test instance (scripts/dev_instance.sh, §14.3a, OPERATIONS §10a) --------------------
# Read from the shell environment by that script, not from this file — nothing here is sourced by a
# script (compose reads this file; the scripts do not). Listed so the knobs are discoverable, with
# the defaults each one overrides.
#
# Do NOT set RESTAURANT_PUBLIC_ORIGIN above for a dev_instance.sh run. That script derives the
# origin from the tunnel hostname and exports it, and the process environment beats this file, so a
# pinned value here is ignored and only succeeds in making this file disagree with what is served.
# What cloudflared points at, and what readiness is probed on. An IPv4 literal, not a name: the web
# port above is published on 127.0.0.1 and nowhere else, and BusyBox wget does not try a second
# address when the first refuses (F-56).
# TUNNEL_TARGET=http://127.0.0.1:8080
# TUNNEL_URL_WAIT=120
# How long postgres is given to accept a connection, and the application to answer /healthz/ready.
# Both waits end EARLY when the thing they are waiting for has stopped, so these are ceilings for a
# slow host rather than the time a broken bring-up takes to report itself (F-55).
# DEV_INSTANCE_DATABASE_WAIT=180
# DEV_INSTANCE_READY_WAIT=300
# How many times a stopped container is started again before `up` gives up on it, and how many engine
# restarts count as a crash loop. Both are the early exits above.
# DEV_INSTANCE_START_ATTEMPTS=3
# DEV_INSTANCE_CRASH_LOOP_RESTARTS=3
# Log lines printed per container when a bring-up fails, and by `dev_instance.sh diagnose`.
# DEV_INSTANCE_LOG_TAIL=40
# How long `up` re-probes the PUBLIC origin before releasing the terminal. The point is that the
# terminal is released on evidence rather than on a return code; 0 disables the check.
# DEV_INSTANCE_SETTLE_SECONDS=20
# DEV_INSTANCE_TUNNEL_CONTAINER=myrestaurant_quicktunnel
# DEV_INSTANCE_STATE_DIRECTORY=${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/myrestaurant
# Fully qualified, for the same reason as DRILL_POSTGRES_IMAGE above and every image in
# compose.yaml (F-51): a short name needs an unqualified-search registry list that Debian does not
# ship populated.
# CLOUDFLARED_IMAGE=docker.io/cloudflare/cloudflared:latest
# Stamped into the image as a build argument and reported by /source (§11.9). dev_instance.sh
# defaults it to `git rev-parse HEAD`, so a tester's bug report names a commit.
# SOURCE_REVISION=
